value.body: A process design engineer works out, on paper and in software, how a new plant or plant expansion will be built — which equipment is needed, what size, and how it all connects. Engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) companies, design consultancies and the project wings of large process companies hire them. A day is office-based: running simulations, drafting and checking documents, and coordinating with mechanical, piping and instrumentation teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. or M.Tech in Chemical

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Aspen HYSYS / Aspen Plus-type simulators, Excel, P&ID tools

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join EPC and consulting firms as graduate or trainee engineers through campus placement or direct hiring. Some firms prefer an M.Tech, and some engineers move here after a few years in plant operations. A short course in process simulation can help at shortlisting.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working with design codes and client specifications

value.title: At a glance
items: Project deadlines drive the workload, with busy and quiet phases.
Common next roles: senior or lead process engineer, process package lead, project engineering.
Work for overseas projects is common at larger EPC firms.
